contract.proof: The host delegates semantics then projects terminal effects/layout without scanning another component owner.
contract.adversarialWitness: Maximum canonical domain with every emitted command projected to the screen owner.

fullScan.rationale: Current canonical transitions may validate a full domain; terminal may not duplicate that semantic scan.

contract.proof: A full screen projection touches each bounded cell and emits its grapheme/appearance state.
contract.adversarialWitness: Every screen cell contains a distinct styled grapheme.

fullScan.rationale: A requested full screen output has row-by-column size.

assumptions: Raw input is a string array with ordinary array iteration; each element read is O(1).
The bound covers row snapshot ownership; diff comparison and terminal serialization are separate operations.
ceilings: One array of rRow immutable string references per accepted raw frame; retained until replacement or close.
deterministicWork: Each raw row is read exactly once per render, including successive renders of the same caller array.
A closed writer reads zero input rows and emits zero output.
contract.resourceRationale: The writer owns one retained row snapshot. Raw input allocates one shallow array; strings are shared by value. Structured frames reuse their freshly serialized rows. close releases the retained snapshot.
contract.proof: createTerminalScreenWriter copies and freezes raw row references before any output callback. Diffing and retained history use that snapshot, so caller mutation cannot change a published frame. The copy is one pass over rRow rows.
contract.adversarialWitness: Successive renders of the same accessor-backed array at 1k, 10k, and 100k rows count exactly rRow caller reads per render; mutation and truncation between renders still update and clear the affected rows.

fullScan.rationale: A mutable caller-owned row array requires one complete shallow snapshot to isolate the previous frame.

variables.name: lInput
variables.meaning: data listeners on the borrowed TTY at removal
variables.ceiling: application-owned listener count plus one adapter forwarder

resources.listeners: one source data listener while connected; zero owned source listeners after close
resources.timers: no adapter timer; a Node escape timeout may finish on the detached private decoder

assumptions: The borrowed stream follows Node ReadStream and EventEmitter contracts; its data listeners remain externally owned.
Node retains its existing byte decoding semantics and escape timeout on one private Readable per active keyboard.
deterministicWork: One active keyboard and one source data forwarder per TTY; no decoder properties or keypress listeners are added to that TTY.
Each chunk is forwarded synchronously once without a second buffering queue; Node decoding and key normalization retain their input/output bounds.
Close detaches the forwarder, clears private listeners and the application callback, destroys the private readable, and releases ownership even if raw restoration throws.
Repeated close and captured stale data callbacks perform zero decoding or publication.
contract.resourceRationale: The caller stream retains only one adapter data callback until close. External decoders are untouched. Node's pending escape work can retain only the detached private decoder after its listener is removed, not the application callback or input stream.
contract.proof: Removing one source data listener can scan lInput listeners. All other adapter teardown steps touch a fixed private listener set and scalar ownership state. Normal input adds one constant synchronous forwarding dispatch per chunk; no subscriber-domain scan or byte copy is introduced by the bridge.
contract.adversarialWitness: 64 acquire/close cycles cover all raw/flow baselines and verify zero residual decoding. Active, idle, and subsequently installed external decoders keep their listener identities. Fragmented UTF-8/escape input, mid-chunk close, late escape completion, setup failures, and a real Linux ReadStream exercise the public factory.

fullScan.rationale: Only the adapter's own source listener and private decoder resources are removed.
